'''''Carex flacca''''', with common names '''blue sedge''', '''gray carex''', '''glaucous sedge''',  or '''carnation-grass''', (syn. '''''Carex glauca'''''), is a species of [[sedge]] native to parts of [[Europe]] and [[North Africa]].<ref name="blue">[http://www.bluestem.ca/carex-flacca.htm Bluestem.ca: ''Carex flacca'' (Blue Sedge)]. accessed 11.30.2011</ref> It is frequent in a range of habitats, including [[grassland]]s, [[moorland]]s, exposed and disturbed soil, and the upper edges of [[salt marsh]]es.<ref name="blue"/> It has [[Naturalisation (biology)|naturalized]] in eastern [[North America]].<ref name="blue"/>

==Description==
''Carex flacca'' leaves are blue-green above, glaucous beneath, to {{convert|6|-|12|in|cm}} in height. The arching leaves are about as long as the inflorescence, {{convert|12|-|16|in|cm}}. The plant spreads in expanding clumps by lateral shoots rooting.<ref name="blue"/> Most stems have two male spikes, close together and often looking like one at first glance. Fruits are {{convert|2|–|2.5|mm|2}}, roundish, with a very short beak, under {{convert|0.3|mm}}. They are densely packed on the spike, not loose and gappy like ''[[Carex panicea]]''. Female spikes are approximately {{convert|2|–|4|cm|1}} long and {{convert|4|–|6|mm}} wide. Female spikes are typically two, and can be short-stalked and upright, or longer-stalked and nodding.

==Cultivation==
''Carex flacca'' is cultivated by [[plant nursery|plant nurseries]] as an [[ornamental plant]], planted for accent or as a [[groundcover]] in [[garden]]s and public landscapes.<ref>[http://www.smgrowers.com/search/basesearch.asp?strSearchText=Carex+flacca&x=9&y=9 San Marcos Growers]</ref> It is also used in [[xeriscape|drought tolerant landscaping]] and erosion control plantings.<ref name="blue"/> It grows in sun to part shade settings.
